To date, businesses operating on HighLevel have generated over $7 billion in ecosystem value, demonstrating the impact of shared infrastructure at scale. By centralizing conversations, automation and intelligence into one system, we help businesses move faster, reduce complexity and execute efficiently.

Behind the platform, HighLevel powers more than 4 billion API hits and 2.5 billion message events daily. With 250 terabytes of distributed data, 250+ microservices and over 1 million domain names supported, our architecture is built for performance, resilience and long-term scalability.

Our people

With over 2,000 team members across 10+ countries, HighLevel operates as a global, remote-first organization built for speed and ownership. We value initiative, clarity and execution, creating space for ambitious people to build systems that support millions of businesses worldwide. Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home.

Our impact

Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We’re proud to be a part of that.

Learn more about us on our YouTube Channel or Blog Posts

About the Role:

We’re looking for a Senior Software Development Engineer (Full Stack) to join our Agency Module, Platform Billing, and Onboarding team. These products form a critical part of HighLevel’s Agency ecosystem, enabling agencies to seamlessly create and manage their accounts, onboard onto the platform, manage subscriptions and billing, and scale their businesses.

Today, 100K+ agencies use HighLevel, collectively serving 2M+ businesses of all sizes, primarily SMBs. The systems we build support critical parts of the agency lifecycle and directly contribute to agency growth by making onboarding, account management, and billing experiences reliable and seamless.

The team builds and scales key capabilities across Agency Signup and Company Management, Platform Billing, and Agency Onboarding. Our onboarding experiences help new agencies get started with HighLevel, configure their accounts, discover and adopt key platform capabilities, and move from signup to successfully using the platform. Together, these systems provide the foundation for agencies to onboard, operate, and grow their businesses on HighLevel.

As an Sr. SDE, you’ll play a key role in building and evolving these systems across the frontend and backend, while contributing to technical architecture and engineering decisions. You’ll work on challenges involving scalable APIs and services, distributed systems, data architecture and modern frontend experiences — with a strong focus on reliability, scalability, and performance.

You’ll collaborate closely with Product Managers, Designers, and other Engineers to take features from requirements and technical planning through implementation and production, while contributing to technical decisions and continuously improving the systems you own.

- Own and contribute to the architecture, design, and development of key product areas across the Agency Module, Agency Onboarding, and Platform Billing.

- Drive technical decisions, identify risks and trade-offs, and independently own complex features from technical design through production.
- Leverage AI-first development practices and AI-assisted development tools to improve development, testing, debugging, and refactoring while maintaining strong quality and security standards.
- Design data models and build efficient queries across data stores such as Firestore, MongoDB, ClickHouse, and Elasticsearch.

- Write clean, efficient, secure, and testable code with appropriate unit and integration test coverage.
- Build and maintain effective observability through logs, metrics, monitoring, and tracing to improve system reliability and enable faster production issue resolution.
- Participate in code reviews, technical design discussions, incident resolution, and operational support, including on-call responsibilities where applicable.
- Collaborate closely with Product Managers, Designers, and other Engineering teams to translate business requirements into scalable technical solutions.
- Follow engineering best practices around security, scalability, maintainability, testing, documentation, and production readiness.

Requirements

- 4+ years of hands-on software engineering experience building and scaling robust backend systems and high-performance frontend applications.
- Strong backend engineering skills with hands-on experience in Node.js, TypeScript, API development, data modeling, and system design. Experience with NestJS is preferred.
- Strong understanding of RESTful API design, microservices architecture, distributed systems, and cross-service communication.
- Hands-on experience working with data stores such as MongoDB and Redis, with a strong understanding of data modeling, query design, and performance optimization.
- Experience working with event-driven architectures and messaging systems such as GCP Pub/Sub, Kafka, RabbitMQ, or similar technologies.
- Exposure to AI/LLM application development, such as integrating LLM APIs, prompt/context design, or building AI-assisted product workflows.
- Good frontend development experience with modern frameworks such as Vue.js, React, or Angular, with Vue.js preferred, along with a good understanding of component-driven architecture and modern CSS frameworks such as Tailwind CSS or Bootstrap.
- Experience with frontend state management patterns and libraries such as Vuex/Pinia, Redux, MobX, or similar solutions.
- Good understanding of production observability and debugging, including logging, monitoring, tracing, error tracking, and performance profiling using tools such as Grafana, Prometheus, Sentry, or similar platforms.
- Experience with modern SDLC practices, Agile development methodologies, Git workflows, automated testing, and CI/CD pipelines.
- Familiarity with specialized data platforms such as ClickHouse and Elasticsearch, and an understanding of when to use document databases, analytical/columnar databases, and search engines.
- Familiarity with modern developer productivity tools, including hands-on experience with AI-assisted development tools such as Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or similar tools.
- Strong problem-solving and debugging skills, with the ability to investigate issues across frontend, backend, databases, integrations, and distributed services.

title: Technical Lead
description:
About Lila Games:
Lila Games strives to build a world-class engineering team (eventually) that can compete with the best in the world. We are a long way from that ambition, but we hope to find others to help us build this team from Bangalore, India. Built in India, published to the world.
More information about Lila: https://tr.ee/7DD-CnUfci

Why This Role Exists:
We are a multi-game studio, and our biggest constraint is how fast we can ship new games. We need a Tech Lead who helps us ship new games faster, both by working directly on the games and by building the shared systems and tooling that multiple projects reuse.
This is a full-stack, full-lifecycle role. The work spans backend and frontend, in Unity, Godot, or whatever a project uses. You should be comfortable picking up new tech stacks fast. You will not be boxed into one engine or one game.

What You Will Own:
- Build shared foundations and systems: Design the systems and tooling that multiple projects reuse, so new games start from a stronger base instead of rebuilding the same things each time.
- Build for liveops operability from day one: Every feature you ship should be operable without engineering involvement after launch. Designers should be able to adjust weapon balance, drop rates, event timing, and economy levers through config or dashboards, not by filing engineering tickets. Think about who operates what you build, not just whether it works on launch day.
- Design scalable features: Architect features that hold up as a game grows in players and content, and that work across projects rather than being rebuilt each time.
- Build testable systems, not just tested systems: Pure logic (economy calculations, matchmaking, config parsing, anything that does not touch the engine) should be unit tested. Gameplay systems should be designed so their logic can be validated without running the full game. You do not need TDD dogma everywhere, but you must know what to test, what not to test, and how to architect so testing is possible.
- Own features end to end across projects: Take features from scoping to shipped, across backend and frontend, often on more than one game at a time. Translate requirements into well-scoped engineering tasks with realistic estimates, in collaboration with product and design.
- Lead and mentor the engineering team in Bangalore: Most engineers have not received structured technical feedback. Code review is your primary mentorship tool: specific, technical, and instructive. Your goal is to raise the floor of every engineer around you.

Working With AI:
You should be comfortable building with AI agents as part of your normal workflow:
- Agentic coding: using AI agents to write and ship code day to day.
- Agentic loops with guardrails: setting up workflows where agents do real work within constraints and checks you define.
- Self-healing agent loops: workflows that detect their own failures and correct themselves.

What We Are Looking For:
We care more about depth of skill and quality of thinking than years of experience. Here is what actually matters:
- Strong engineering fundamentals: you understand SOLID principles and can explain why they matter in the context of a game codebase, specifically why they make live-ops changes safer and faster, not just cleaner.
- Full-stack and quick with new stacks: you are comfortable across backend and frontend (Unity, React, or whatever a project uses) and you pick up unfamiliar tech stacks fast.
- Hands-on agentic coder: you write code day to day and use AI agents to do it. You are comfortable with agentic loops and the guardrails that keep them reliable. This is not a management-from-a-distance role.
- Liveops systems thinking: you have worked on a live game and understand what it means to build features that can be tuned, toggled, or updated without a full build. You think about config, feature flags, and content pipelines as engineering concerns, not product team problems.
- Mentorship instinct: you give direct, specific technical feedback. You can explain not just what is wrong but why and how to fix it.
- High agency: you identify problems and propose solutions without waiting to be asked. You own outcomes, not tasks.
Unity proficiency is a bonus. Backend or networking experience is valuable given the multiplayer games that we work on.

What We Are Not Looking For:
- Engineers who equate years of experience with expertise. We have seen too many senior engineers with bad habits and too many sharp 4-year engineers who outperform them.
- People who profile only when performance is already broken. By then it is too late.
- Engineers who build features without thinking about who operates them post-launch. Liveops operability is an engineering responsibility.
- People who prefer to manage from a distance. We need someone in the code.

Application Process:
Apply: submit your resume. We respond within 3 business days.
Written Assignment: we send this first, a focused technical problem designed to surface how you think, not just what you know. You may use AI tools, but you must fully understand what you submit.
First Interview: a combined screening and technical and cultural conversation with our leadership team.
Final Interview: a conversation with a founder, including a walkthrough of your assignment.
Offer: formal offer with compensation details.
Please review our company values at https://bit.ly/3rsN1ti before applying. Cultural fit is not a formality here. It is a filter.

HighLevel is an AI-powered business operating system that gives agencies, entrepreneurs and SMBs the infrastructure to build, automate and scale. Today, HighLevel supports SMBs across 150+ countries, fueling community-driven growth rooted in real customer outcomes.

To date, businesses operating on HighLevel have generated over $7 billion in ecosystem value, demonstrating the impact of shared infrastructure at scale. By centralizing conversations, automation and intelligence into one system, we help businesses move faster, reduce complexity and execute efficiently.

Behind the platform, HighLevel powers more than 4 billion API hits and 2.5 billion message events daily. With 250 terabytes of distributed data, 250+ microservices and over 1 million domain names supported, our architecture is built for performance, resilience and long-term scalability.

Our People

With over 2,000 team members across 10+ countries, HighLevel operates as a global, remote-first organization built for speed and ownership. We value initiative, clarity and execution, creating space for ambitious people to build systems that support millions of businesses worldwide. Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home.

Our Impact

Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We’re proud to be a part of that.

Learn more about us on our YouTube Channel or Blog Posts .

About the Role:

We're looking for a Staff Front-End Engineer to own the architecture of our platform UI. This is a core platform role, not a feature role — you'll own the layer every other team builds on: the application shell, our module federation topology, the shared component library, build tooling, and the performance bar that applies across every surface of the product. You'll stay hands-on with code and architecture while setting technical direction across multiple teams and leading multi-quarter migrations without stalling feature delivery. Our stack is primarily Vue 3; strong engineers from React, Angular, or Svelte backgrounds are welcome, and existing Vue experience is a plus.

Responsibilities:

- Failure Isolation: Design so a broken or slow remote degrades one surface, not the whole application — with fallbacks, timeouts, and the observability to identify which remote caused an incident.
- Release Strategy: Own the deployment and versioning story for independent releases, including contract testing across host/remote boundaries, staged rollout, and fast rollback of a single remote.
- Load Performance: Attack bundle size and dependency-graph bloat through code splitting, shared-chunk strategy across federated remotes, preloading/prefetching, and caching/CDN strategy.
- Runtime Performance: Attack main-thread cost through long-task analysis, reactivity and re-render cost, list virtualization, and memory leak diagnosis in long-lived sessions. You're the person engineers escalate production-only regressions and render thrash to.
- Performance Measurement: Define the metrics that matter (Core Web Vitals, INP, route transition time), instrument them in real-user monitoring, and enforce budgets in CI so regressions are caught before they ship.
- Quality Bar: Set and enforce accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA), internationalization, and cross-browser support through automated checks, not documentation alone.
- Technical Leadership: Write proposals that build genuine consensus, review designs and code where decisions are expensive to reverse, and mentor senior and mid-level engineers across the org.

Requirements:

- 9+ years of front-end development experience. 
- Expert-level JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, and CSS, with a first-principles understanding of the browser — rendering/layout, the event loop, network/caching, and memory.
- Deep production experience with a modern component framework. Primarily Vue 3 (Composition API); strong React, Angular, or Svelte experience is welcome if you're willing to go deep on Vue.
- Demonstrated architectural ownership — you've defined a front-end architecture and moved a real codebase from one state to another without freezing feature work.
- Hands-on production experience with micro-frontends or module federation, including the failure modes. Equivalent experience decomposing a large monolith by other means also considered.
- Proven track record optimizing large-scale, complex web applications. Be ready to walk through a specific example with numbers.
- Experience with modern build tooling at scale (Vite, Webpack, Rspack, Turborepo, or Nx), with enough depth to debug the build when it breaks.
- Working knowledge of accessibility as an engineering discipline — semantics, focus/keyboard behavior, ARIA where genuinely needed, screen reader testing.
- Strong written communication. On a remote-first, async team, most of your influence travels as design docs, RFCs, and PR descriptions.
- A track record of mentoring engineers and driving change across teams you don't manage.
- Nice to have: familiarity with Node.js, server-side rendering, and open-source contributions.

What You'll Lead:

- The target architecture for our front-end, and the migrations that get us there — sequenced into reversible steps, driven with codemods and adoption metrics, agreed across teams rather than imposed on them.
- The application shell and its contracts: bootstrapping, routing, auth-aware navigation, error and loading boundaries, and cross-application state.
- Our module federation topology: host and remote boundaries, shared dependency and singleton management, and version skew between independently deployed remotes.
- The shared component library and design system implementation, with APIs that are hard to misuse and safe to version.

**Who Are We?**  
  
Postman is the world’s leading API platform, used by more than 45 million+ developers and 500,000 organizations, including 98% of the Fortune 500. Postman is helping developers and professionals across the globe build the API-first world by simplifying each step of the API lifecycle and streamlining collaboration—enabling users to create better APIs, faster.
  
  
The company is headquartered in San Francisco and has offices in Boston, New York, Austin, Tokyo, London, and Bangalore - where Postman was founded. Postman is privately held, with funding from Battery Ventures, BOND, Coatue, CRV, Insight Partners, and Nexus Venture Partners. Learn more at postman.com or connect with Postman on X via @getpostman.
  
  
P.S: We highly recommend reading The "API-First World" graphic novel to understand the bigger picture and our vision at Postman.

  

About the Team
  
The Identity and Access Management team is responsible for building a secure, reliable, and seamless identity platform for all Postman users. This team owns the systems behind authentication, session management, access control, service accounts, invites, and other foundational identity capabilities that power the product.
  
Postman’s identity layer is a critical part of the product experience. It sits on the path of every authenticated request and enables users, teams, and systems to access Postman securely and collaborate effectively. The team works on a mix of core platform improvements, new product capabilities, and reliability/security investments.
  
  
What You’ll Do

* Build and maintain backend systems that power Postman’s identity and authentication platform.
* Work with Product, Design, and Engineering teams to scope, implement, test, and launch new features and platform improvements.
* Contribute to the design and development of scalable, reliable services and APIs.
* Improve system quality by writing tests, fixing bugs, and strengthening observability and monitoring.
* Participate in production support, debugging, incident investigation, and follow-through on fixes.
* Work on performance, scalability, and reliability improvements for the services owned by the team.
* Take ownership of well-defined projects and components, and drive them with support from senior engineers and your manager.
* Contribute to code reviews and team discussions, and adopt strong software engineering practices.
Collaborate with other engineers to break down work, resolve ambiguity, and deliver iteratively.  

About You

* You have **2+ years of experience** building backend or distributed systems in production environments.
* You have a solid foundation in software engineering fundamentals such as data structures, algorithms, networking, and system design basics.
* You are comfortable writing clean, testable, maintainable code.
* You have experience working with backend services, APIs, and databases.
* You are able to work through ambiguity with guidance and ask the right questions to move work forward.
* You care about quality, reliability, and learning how systems behave in production.
* You collaborate well with engineers, product managers, and other stakeholders.
* You have good written and verbal communication skills.
You are curious, eager to learn, and motivated to grow in a platform engineering environment.  

Technical Experience We Value

* Experience with backend technologies such as **Node.js, Java, Python, Go, or Ruby**
* Familiarity with **distributed systems** and **cloud infrastructure**
* Experience building or maintaining **microservices** and APIs
* Familiarity with **databases, caching, queues, or event-driven systems**
* Exposure to **testing, monitoring, debugging, and production support**
* Familiarity with **authentication, authorization, identity, RBAC, access control, or security-sensitive systems** is a plus, but not required

  

**What Else?**
--------------

  

In addition to Postman's pay-on-performance philosophy, and a flexible schedule working with a fun, collaborative team, Postman offers a comprehensive set of benefits, including full medical coverage, flexible PTO, wellness reimbursement, and a monthly lunch stipend. Along with that, our wellness programs will help you stay in the best of your physical and mental health.  - Build Self-Service Platform Capabilities: Develop internal tooling, abstractions, and automated workflows that empower other engineering teams to self-serve their infrastructure needs, significantly reducing operational bottlenecks and manual intervention.
